gaps.fact: The Court's bands, Salta 1500 to 2000 metres and the highest in Argentina, Mendoza 600 to 1200 metres: the Codex gives truer but different figures (Cafayate 1,700 m, the upper valley past 3,000 m, Gualtallary at 1,600 m), and never states the Court's Mendoza band, so a candidate cannot match the printed answer.

Torrontés commonly sees no oak, while new or used, French or American oak is common for Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon: only a Régionale grape card and two articles say so; no chapter fact or question.
Chardonnay as Argentina's second white: no question or chapter names it for Argentina; only the mendoza and argentina articles do.
Cabernet Sauvignon as Argentina's second Court red: never asked for Argentina and absent from both chapters; the articles carry it in the cortes with Malbec.
Tempranillo, a Certified red in Argentina: it appears nowhere in the Codex's Argentine material except in the trap that Argentine La Rioja has no Tempranillo tradition.
85 per cent minimum to name a grape variety on the label: articles only; Classifications & Labels fact 6 lists the percentages of every New World country but Argentina, and no question asks it.

Torrontés has medium plus to high acidity, which the Court calls unique among aromatic varieties, and soapy, floral and fruity flavours: the Codex grades its acid medium to medium plus (GRAPES) and 2 of 3 on the Régionale card, and never uses soapy; it does say Muscat and Gewürztraminer carry less acid.
Vineyards revitalised by Italian and Spanish immigrants: the country overview has it (the railway of 1885), but no question or chapter.
Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon with steak and chimichurri: chimichurri appears nowhere in the Codex, and no question pairs Malbec with anything.

courtUpdates.printed: IG: Indicación Geográficas, GIs in English; DOC: Denominación de Origen Controlada system
courtUpdates.now: The tiers are unchanged, but the INV keeps registering IGs: Tamberías, Hilario and Sorocayense in San Juan's Calingasta Valley (INV resolutions 35, 36 and 37 of 2023, reported in February 2024) and Valle de Pucará in Salta (reported in April 2025). The country ladder names Paraje Altamira, Los Chacayes and San Pablo and none of the newer IGs.
courtUpdates.source: Search: Los Andes, 7 February 2024 (three Calingasta IGs); Marval O'Farrell Mairal, 4 April 2025 (Valle de Pucará).

notes: Mapped questions: South America holds Régionale 60 and Village 23, 83 in all, shared with Chile; Argentine stems are Régionale 26 and Village 9 (35), Chile 37 and Uruguay and Brazil 11 of the rest. Outside the mapped cats, i-6pj6n9u8 and c-ud8xt1sq (Producers & Icons), i-kbvqvdcf and i-le57zcor (Geography & Maps), i-i2e7xewx (Grapes & Labels), i-je3qjikm (Loire) and c-wusonuuh (Italy North) touch Argentina. The Régionale side is rich: the acequias, Luján de Cuyo's DOC of 1989 and San Rafael, the Uco's departments and Gualtallary, Maipú, the Zonda, hail nets, Salta and the Calchaquí Valleys, Pouget's 1853 cuttings, Torrontés' parents, Bonarda as Douce Noire, ultraviolet light and skins, the pink Criollas. The Village bank's nine Argentine stems lean to geology and the far south (caliche, Paraje Altamira, Chubut) and leave the Court's Certified cells thin: Tempranillo, the 85 per cent rule, the immigrants, chimichurri, and Cabernet and Chardonnay as Argentine grapes are untaught. The Court's service row is met only by the general decanting rule (Service & Hospitality fact 4, c-wgifeyxj and the decanting table), which is enough in principle. The Court's Andes "an average of 900 meters" reads as a vineyard height rather than the range's, and its Indicación Geográficas mixes singular and plural; the Codex follows neither slip. One factual error: Douce Noir for Douce Noire in the Village chapter. House rule note for the owner: c-m9k8c5xn, filed in this shared category, names a living winemaker in its explanation. One search spent (new IGs since 2023); the second was not needed. Reviewed again in this pass: every cited id exists in its stated category, the 26 and 9 Argentine stems were recounted, the error and each gap were rechecked against the chapters, the grape cards and the argentina sheet, and the article questions (r- ids) were added where they meet a row.
